### data-firehose-at-least-once-duplicates-except-s3-iceberg-snowflake

**Claim.** Amazon Data Firehose uses at-least-once semantics for delivery, so retries after a timeout can introduce duplicates. This applies to all destination types except Amazon S3, Apache Iceberg Tables and Snowflake.

**Write it as.** `at-least-once semantics for data delivery` · `except for Amazon S3 destinations, Apache Iceberg Tables, and Snowflake destinations`

**Scope.** duplicates possible when a delivery times out and the original request eventually goes through.

> "Amazon Data Firehose uses at-least-once semantics for data delivery. In some circumstances, such as when data delivery times out, delivery retries by Amazon Data Firehose might introduce duplicates if the original data-delivery request eventually goes through. This applies to all destination types that Amazon Data Firehose supports, except for Amazon S3 destinations, Apache Iceberg Tables, and Snowflake destinations."
> — [Understand data delivery in Amazon Data Firehose](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/basic-deliver.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-15.

### data-firehose-backup-buffer-1-128-mib-60-900-seconds

**Claim.** Amazon Data Firehose uses Amazon S3 to back up all data or only failed data, and buffers incoming data before it backs it up to Amazon S3. For this backup you can choose a buffer size of 1–128 MiBs and a buffer interval of 60–900 seconds; the condition that is satisfied first triggers data delivery to Amazon S3.

**Write it as.** `1–128 MiBs` · `60–900 seconds`

**Scope.** S3 backup buffering hints; maximum; not adjustable; the condition that is satisfied first triggers delivery to Amazon S3.

> "Buffering hints, compression and encryption for backup - Amazon Data Firehose uses Amazon S3 to backup all or failed only data that it attempts to deliver to your chosen destination. Amazon Data Firehose buffers incoming data before delivering it (backing it up) to Amazon S3. You can choose a buffer size of 1–128 MiBs and a buffer interval of 60–900 seconds. The condition that is satisfied first triggers data delivery to Amazon S3."
> — [Configure backup settings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/create-configure-backup.html)

### data-firehose-both-delivery-and-backup-fail-pauses-stream

### data-firehose-buffer-grows-when-destination-falls-behind

**Claim.** If delivery to the destination falls behind the writing to the Firehose stream, Firehose raises the buffer size dynamically to catch up, which helps ensure that all data is delivered.

### data-firehose-buffer-under-60s-raises-s3-put-cost

### data-firehose-direct-put-auto-increases-limit-on-throttling

**Claim.** If a Direct PUT stream is throttled because ingest exceeds its throughput capacity, Amazon Data Firehose automatically increases the throughput limit of the stream until the throttling is contained. This can take time, so producers should keep retrying the failed records.

**Write it as.** `automatically increases the throughput limit of the stream`

**Scope.** per Direct PUT Firehose stream; if you expect sudden large bursts or need more than the default throughput, request a limit increase.

> "If a Direct PUT stream experiences throttling due to higher data ingest volumes that exceed the throughput capacity of a Firehose stream, Amazon Data Firehose automatically increases the throughput limit of the stream until the throttling is contained. Depending on increased throughput and throttling, it might take longer for Firehose to increase the throughput of a stream to the desired levels. Because of this, continue to retry the failed data ingest records."
